intent: v1.3.3 patch (James 2026-10-09): the app venv's pip (24.0, from Ubuntu's ensurepip) carries 6 advisories (CVE-2025-8869, CVE-2026-3219, CVE-2026-6357, CVE-2026-13346, CVE-2026-8643, CVE-2026-1703; fixed by >=26.2.0) and is outside requirements.lock, so neither apt nor the sca gate covers it. Make pip (and any other venv bootstrap tool) a hash-pinned, locked, scanned dependency like every other package; installer/upgrade/offline bundle install it; add a check that the installed venv holds ONLY locked packages at locked versions. REG-0068.

decisions.approaches: one (lock + install pinned pip; venv drift check)

security.outbound_call: no new (pip wheel comes from PyPI at bundle-build/online install, same as every other wheel)

decisions.standard: James 2026-10-09: make pinning + continuous scanning of EVERY installed app package a standard for all apps, CI pipelines and the OS-update skills (separate follow-up for ci-templates + system-updates).

openproject_note: No ticket: patch on James's direct instruction.

decide.verdict: PATCH on James's direct instruction 2026-10-09 ('lets start workin 1.3.3 specifcally to account for the update'): pin + hash + scan the venv's pip (24.0 -> 26.2.x, 6 advisories), venv-drift check; one defensible approach, no panel (as WO-0005/7/8). Security: no data/route/credential change; no new outbound source.

builder.scope_source: the coordinator's brief (WO had no scout section; brief items 1-8 taken as scout.scope, as WO-0008 did)
builder.root_cause: pip is installed into the app venv by `python3 -m venv` (ensurepip; 24.0 on Ubuntu 24.04), not by any installer step that reads requirements.txt/requirements.lock. Every control in the repo (lock gate, sca, CI Trivy on the lock, the installers' --require-hashes) is keyed to the lock, so a package the venv acquires outside the lock is invisible to all of them; v1.1.0 also deliberately refused to self-upgrade pip because the only upgrade available then was unhashed. Nothing compared the installed venv with the lock.
